PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person shall
make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting a
meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the individual ’s
failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

minutes_text:
AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called the meeting to order at 5:11 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items on the Closed Session agenda. 

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council/Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:12  p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:00 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session item #1.  City staff made a presentation, the City Council provided direction and no reportable action was taken on item #1. 

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called regular City Council meeting to order at 6:02 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Transportation Director McFerguson led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION Mayor Argumedo offered the invocation.

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. Proclamation Declaring September 2024 as Deaf Awareness Month in the City of Commerce Director of Parks and Recreation, Alaniz, gave a detailed presentation. 

Neil Cordova, a speech interpreter for LA County, spoke on the importance of providing access, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. He emphasized the need for accessibility and suggested adding subtitles to Council agenda videos.

Mayor Argumedo then proceeded to read a proclamation.

PUBLIC COMMENT There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items within their jurisdiction. 




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo

5.. Resolution Approving Compensation for Unrepresented Executive Management Employees

8.. Purchase of Additional Public Safety City Radios

6.. Adopting the City’s Title VI Program, and Authorizing Staff to Submit to the Federal Transit Administration for Review and Final Approval

7.. Transportation’s Operational Report for the Fourth Quarter of Fiscal Year 2024

4.. Approval of Minutes

3.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 5A and 5B

SCHEDULED MATTERS

9.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Duarte provided an update covering the past two weeks.

Councilmember Lainez inquired about whether there is a matrix or performance data available on the effectiveness of the newly installed automated license plate readers, particularly in addressing the recent surge of over 20 auto thefts. He requested that this information be included in the bi-weekly Sheriff's report to assess how these tools are benefiting the community.

Mayor Argumedo acknowledged that while automated license plate readers are effective in preventing crime, their use may result in increased visible activity in the community. He emphasized the need for outreach to inform residents that these tools are beneficial in reducing crime and enhancing public safety.

10.. Committee and Commission Appointments Vice Mayor Altamirano appointed Jaelyn Ramirez to the Youth Advisory Commission.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Rebollo thanked the Library Services for organizing a successful College Fair. She also expressed appreciation to Neil Cordova for providing translation during the Deaf Awareness presentation. Councilmember Rebollo requested a calendar of all awareness days and suggested scheduling monthly awareness events at the first meeting of each month. Additionally, she recommended providing resources in libraries, partnering with other departments to promote awareness and events, and ensuring inclusivity for the community.

Councilmember Lainez thanked the Parks and Recreation Department for the successful Fiesta Patrias event and complimented the Ballet Folklorico performance. He also noted that the College Fair was well-attended. On the topic of public safety, Councilmember Lainez requested an update on the pending items from the public safety plan and inquired about the status of current programs.

Vice Mayor Altamirano shared that he attended the Shopping Extravaganza at Citadel Outlets, which was a successful fundraising event supporting Sister City organization. He mentioned receiving numerous calls regarding red curbs and emphasized the need to address this issue. Vice Mayor Altamirano also wished good luck to his colleagues running for re-election.

Mayor Argumedo commented that both the Fiesta Patrias and College Fair were great events. He also expressed his gratitude for the Coffee with Deputies event.


ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 6:41 p.m.

Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.
